types.name: CapsulePlacement
types.doc: Where one proxy capsule is: its centre and a rotation taking +Z to its axis (x, y, z, w).

types.name: FootHold
types.doc:
While the idle pose shows (standing, and the fade into and out of a walk), the feet are held where they stand:
the idle pose keeps its feet still relative to the body, so a body that starts to move drags them, and one that
lowers or rises slides them. Each foot is reached for at the spot it had when the hold began, with a hold that
comes in and goes out smoothly; in a steady walk the gait already keeps a planted foot still. Only a character whose
legs are IK chains can hold its feet.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: How firmly the feet are held where they stand, 0 (free) to 1 (held).

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Lets go of both feet at once.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc: Eases the hold toward what the pose asks for and reaches each held foot to its anchor. `kneeling` turns it off.

types.name: HumanAttachment
types.doc: A rigid object carried by a bone, such as a tool in a hand.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Node that follows the bone; the prop hangs beneath it.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: Transform of the prop in the bone's frame.

types.name: HumanBody
types.doc:
Animation and locomotion state shared by every action in a worker's job.

The body is what actions talk to: where it stands, which limbs reach or carry, how the hands
grip, how far the upper body leans. Each limb keeps its own small state machine
(`LimbControl`); the body steps them, solves wrist goals against the animated pose, and turns
the tuning in `HumanPosture` into the pose. See BODY.md for how the layers fit together.

fields.name: palmReach
fields.doc:
How far the point a hand holds with (between the wrist and the knuckles) is beyond its wrist, in metres. The
arm has to bring the wrist this much less far than the point it is reaching for.

fields.name: grip
fields.doc: True between a completed pick and its matching place.

fields.name: standingBone
fields.doc:
Where a bone stands when the body is upright and at rest, in model space, for planning where to
stand: the animated pose bobs with the gait, so reading it at the instant a plan is made would let
a reach near the limit be possible in one phase of a stride and not another.

fields.name: graspDepth
fields.doc:
How far an object reaches from the palm, straight out along the palm's normal, for the hand that
is about to close on it: the fingers must curl down that far. `object` is the object's box.

fields.name: setGrasp
fields.doc: Closes a hand's fingers around an object that reaches `depth` metres from the palm, and keeps them so while it holds it.

fields.name: grasp
fields.doc: The curl each finger closes to around what a hand holds (THUMB to PINKY), or null when it holds nothing shaped.

fields.name: fingerDepth
fields.doc:
How far a fingertip is from the palm along the palm's normal, in metres: positive on the palm's
side, where an object is held. Zero for a hand without that finger.

fields.name: setLean
fields.doc: Where the torso is asked to lean; it eases there. Zero stands upright.

fields.name: canCrouch
fields.doc: Whether the character can crouch: its asset has a crouch clip to lower the body with.

fields.name: setCrouch
fields.doc: Where the body is asked to crouch (0 stands, 1 is the clip's full crouch); it eases there.

fields.name: crouchAmount
fields.doc: How far the body is into its crouch now.

fields.name: setArmsDown
fields.doc:
Holds the arms that are not reaching or carrying down at the sides instead of letting the gait swing them,
so walking up to a surface does not sweep a hand across what lies on it. Eases in and out like the hang a
lean asks for. Pick and Place let go of it once their hand has the part.

fields.name: leanReached
fields.doc: Whether the body has finished easing to the lean it was asked for.

fields.name: setHinge
fields.doc: Where the body is asked to bend at the hips, on top of its lean; it eases there. Zero stands straight.

fields.name: crouchReached
fields.doc: Whether the body has finished easing to the crouch it was asked for.

fields.name: canKneel
fields.doc: Whether the character can kneel: its asset has a kneeling clip to lower the body onto a knee with.

fields.name: setKneel
fields.doc:
Where the body is asked to kneel (0 stands, 1 the lowest the kneeling clip goes); it eases there. A kneel and a crouch are
different ways down, so a body kneels only from standing: ask for a crouch of nothing first.

fields.name: kneelAmount
fields.doc: How far the body is into its kneel now.

fields.name: downReached
fields.doc: Whether the body has finished easing to the crouch and the kneel it was asked for.

fields.name: downAmount
fields.doc: How far down, in either way, the body is now: 0 standing.

fields.name: crouchShift
fields.doc:
How far a bone sits from where it stands upright when the body crouches `amount`, in model space.
Measured on the skeleton at the current animation time, with no lean; the pose is left as it was.

fields.name: kneelShift
fields.doc: The same for a kneel: how far a bone sits from standing when the body kneels `amount`.

fields.name: leanFor
fields.doc:
The lean that carries a hand's shoulder `shift` metres further forward, and the shift it can
deliver (less than asked when that would pass the posture's maximum lean). Measured by leaning
the skeleton a test amount, so it holds for any rig; the pose is left as it was. `crouch` is the
depth the body is planned to be at, since a crouched torso carries the shoulder differently.

fields.name: hingeFor
fields.signature: (hand:HumanLimb, shift:Float, crouch:Float, kneel:Float, lean:Float, ?belly:HumanBone):{angle:Float, shift:Float, drop:Float, belly:Float}
fields.doc:
The same for bending at the hips, on top of a lean already planned (`lean`): the hinge that carries the shoulder `shift`
metres further forward than that lean does, and the shift and drop it delivers, up to the posture's maximum hinge.

fields.name: setReachModel
fields.doc: Legacy model-space reach target used by HumanReachTask.

fields.name: setReachShoulder
fields.doc:
Reaches for a point given as an offset from the limb's shoulder (model-space axes), so the target moves with the
shoulder: the arm keeps its shape as the body leans, straightens, and walks. A caller whose offset should turn
with the torso turns it itself, by the change in `torsoPitch`.

fields.name: shoulderPosition
fields.doc: Where a limb's shoulder is, in model space.

fields.name: chestPosition
fields.doc: Where the chest is, in model space (the pelvis on a rig without one).

fields.name: reachTargetModel
fields.doc: A limb's reach target in model space, whichever frame it was given in.

fields.name: footHold
fields.doc: How firmly the feet are held where they stand, 0 (free) to 1 (held).

fields.name: torsoPitch
fields.doc: How far the upper body is pitched forward now, in radians: the lean and the hip hinge together.

fields.name: setHeldPoint
fields.doc: Predicted world position of the object reference point held by a hand.

fields.name: gripPoint
fields.doc:
World position of a hand's palm centre, midway between the wrist and the
middle-finger knuckle (the wrist itself on a rig without fingers). Pick
brings this point to its grasp point.

fields.name: reachFailure
fields.doc: Why a wrist goal is beyond 95% of the arm's length from its shoulder, or null.

fields.name: solveReach
fields.signature: (hand:HumanLimb, target:Array<Float>, point:() -> Array<Float>, guess:Array<Float>, cap:Float):{goal:Array<Float>, error:Float, failure:Null<String>}
fields.doc:
Finds the wrist goal that brings point() onto target with the arm at full
IK weight, re-evaluating the pose at the current animation time between
attempts, so nothing accumulates across frames. Each attempt steps the
best goal so far by the remaining miss; a step that does not improve on it
is halved instead of taken, so the returned error never exceeds the
guess's and repeated solves cannot oscillate. guess is the first wrist
goal; the goal never moves more than cap metres from it. Leaves the arm
reaching for the returned goal. failure is set only when the guess itself
is out of reach; steps beyond reach are treated as overshoots.

fields.name: travelToAnimation
fields.doc:
How far a limb's wrist would travel, in metres, if its reach were let go now: the distance from where
the IK holds it to where its animation puts it. The pose is left as it was.

fields.name: wristWorld
fields.doc: Where a hand's wrist is in the world now.

fields.name: blendSeconds
fields.doc:
How long a reach takes to blend in from the animation or out to it, given how far the wrist has to go: at
least `minimum`, and longer when the distance would otherwise push the wrist past the posture's blend speed.
Easing peaks at half as much again as the average speed, hence the factor.

fields.name: carryTargetModel
fields.doc: Current carry target in model space, tied to the animated chest.

fields.name: standingTwist
fields.doc:
How far the idle pose's shoulders are twisted from square to the way the body faces, in radians (positive: the left shoulder
further back). A body that faces a table with its shoulders square needs its root turned by the opposite.

fields.name: bodyTurn
fields.doc: How far the body is turned in model space from standing at rest (a turn clip turns it so), in radians.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc:
Returns the body to rest at a floor pose as if newly constructed: no route,
no reach, nothing carried or held, and the idle pose evaluated.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc: Advances gait once, then reapplies current world targets over that pose.

fields.name: evaluate
fields.doc:
Re-evaluates reaches at the current animation time for in-frame IK solving. Nothing here is skinned or shown
(`HumanCharacter.publish` does that). With `present` off the pose is a measurement, for the attempts of a solve
of which only the last is to be kept.

types.name: HumanBodyProxy
types.doc:
A person's collision stand-in: fifteen capsules between standard bones
(head, abdomen, chest, and three segments per limb), sized from a
HumanDescription and placed from a HumanPose every frame. Simulations use it
where the skinned mesh would be too costly to collide with.

fields.name: standard
fields.doc:
The standard proxy for a rig, measured at its rest pose. Radii are
proportions of stature; capsule lengths follow the rig's bones, scaled
by description.scale like the character's visual root.

fields.name: place
fields.doc: Every capsule's placement for a pose, through a root transform (column-major 4x4).

fields.name: rotationFromZ
fields.doc: The rotation (x, y, z, w) taking +Z onto a unit direction by the shortest arc.

types.name: HumanBodyView
types.doc:
Draws a human's collision capsules or skeleton beneath its root node, for
checking a body proxy against the mesh. Bones are rigid, so every part keeps
one geometry and only its node moves; update() places them from a pose in
the character's model space.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Builds hidden capsule and skeleton nodes beneath parent (the character root).

fields.name: show
fields.doc: Shows the capsules, the skeleton, or neither (the mesh alone).

fields.name: update
fields.doc: Places every part from a pose in model space.

types.name: HumanCapsule
types.doc:
One capsule of a body proxy. It runs from its `from` bone towards its `to`
bone, continued past `to` by `extension` times that span (a head beyond its
joint, fingers beyond the knuckles) or stopped `trim` metres short of it (a
shin that leaves the ankle to the foot). The capsule's hemisphere centres sit
at the two ends, so it covers `radius` beyond each.

fields.name: length
fields.doc: Distance between the hemisphere centres, fixed at the rest pose.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (name:String, from:HumanBone, to:HumanBone, extension:Float, trim:Float, radius:Float, length:Float):Void

types.name: HumanCarryPosture
types.doc: Hands held near the chest while the legs keep their walking gait.

types.name: HumanCharacter
types.doc:
An animated humanoid in a SceneKit scene: the skinned mesh, its standard
skeleton pose, and rigid attachments that follow bones. Place it by
transforming root; advance() plays the current clip and moves everything.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Presents asset in scene; the rig is detected from its joint names unless given.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Model height at the rest pose, in metres.

fields.name: attach
fields.doc:
Attaches a rigid prop to a bone. The prop is placed at offset in the
bone's frame (see HumanPose for the hand frame). The prop's asset must
stay live until this call returns.

fields.name: reach
fields.doc:
Reaches a limb's wrist or ankle for target ([x, y, z] in model space)
on top of the animation, from the next advance on. The elbow or knee
points along pole, a model-space direction: by default an elbow bends the
way the animation bends it, which stays continuous wherever the hand goes,
and knees point forward. weight blends from the animation (0) to the
full reach (1). Throws when the rig's limb is not one chain, as with
Quaternius legs, whose feet hang off the body as IK controls.

fields.name: setHandCurl
fields.doc:
Curls a hand's fingers, from open (0) to a fist (1), on top of the animation. A rig without finger
joints ignores it. Takes effect from the next advance.

fields.name: setSpineLean
fields.doc:
Leans the upper body forward by angle radians (0 upright), on top of the animation, by pitching
the spine's upper joints together. Takes effect from the next advance.

fields.name: setSpineHinge
fields.doc:
Bends the body forward at the hips by angle radians (0 upright), on top of the animation and of any lean: the whole trunk
pitches about the lowest spine joint, so the shoulders travel far forward and down, as when someone bends over a table to
reach across it. A rig without that joint ignores it. Takes effect from the next advance.

fields.name: legsAreChains
fields.doc:
Whether the legs are IK chains (thigh, shin and foot one below the other), so a foot can be held where it is.
The bundled worker's feet hang off the body as controls instead, and cannot.

fields.name: canCrouch
fields.doc: Whether the asset has a crouch clip to lower the body with.

fields.name: setCrouch
fields.doc:
Lowers the body toward a crouch, by mixing the asset's crouching clip over the animation: 0 stands, 1 is
the clip's full crouch. The legs and pelvis come from the clip, so the feet stay near the floor (they are not
pinned: one may lift a few centimetres at full depth). Throws when the asset has no crouch clip. A crouch takes the
place of a kneel, as a kneel does of a crouch. Takes effect from the next advance, and is meant for a worker standing still.

fields.name: canKneel
fields.doc: Whether the asset has a kneeling clip to lower the body further with than a crouch can.

fields.name: setKneel
fields.doc:
Lowers the body onto a knee, with the arm reaching down, by holding the going-down part of the asset's kneeling clip
at the point where the pelvis is that fraction of the way down: 0 stands, 1 is the lowest the clip goes. It takes the
place of a crouch (the two are different ways down, not stages of one), so asking for a kneel stands the crouch back up
and the other way round. Throws when the asset has no kneeling clip.

fields.name: setDown
fields.doc: Sets how far down the body is in both ways at once (a kneel, if any, wins); for measuring and putting back.

fields.name: setHandCurls
fields.doc:
Curls each finger of a hand on its own: values are indexed HumanHand.THUMB to PINKY, each 0 open to
1 a fist. A rig without finger joints ignores it.

fields.name: handCurls
fields.doc: How curled each finger of a hand is (THUMB to PINKY), or all zero for a rig without them.

fields.name: fingertip
fields.doc: The model-space position of a finger's tip on a hand (HumanHand.THUMB to PINKY), or null when it has none.

fields.name: handCurl
fields.doc: How curled a hand's fingers are, or 0 for a rig without them.

fields.name: release
fields.doc: Returns a limb to its animation.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc:
Advances the current clip and applies every turn and reach, so `pose` describes the body now. The scene is not
touched: a simulation advances many times for each frame it draws, and skinning and uploading a mesh nobody sees
is the largest cost of doing it. Whoever draws the character calls `publish` once per frame.

fields.name: publish
fields.doc:
Skins the mesh to the state the character is in now and moves it and its attachments in the scene. The state
is the one the latest `advance` left (a measurement puts back what it changes), so a probe between an advance
and a publish cannot reach the screen.

fields.name: probe
fields.doc:
Evaluates the pose as it would be now, at the current animation time and with every turn and reach applied, and
makes `pose` current, without skinning the model or moving attachments. For measuring (what would the shoulder
do under a lean, where would the hand be if released): nothing a measurement poses reaches the scene, and
the next `advance` evaluates the pose again as usual.

fields.name: changedNodes
fields.doc: Nodes whose geometry or world transform changed in the last advance.

types.name: HumanCrouch
types.doc:
A one-way clip of going down into a crouch, measured so that any depth between standing and crouched can be posed
from it: how far the pelvis has dropped at each moment of the clip, as a fraction of its whole drop. Holding the
clip at the time where the drop is a given fraction gives an authored pose at that depth, in place of a blend of
standing and crouching poses.

fields.name: timeFor
fields.doc: The time in the clip at which the body is `depth` of the way down (0 standing, 1 crouched).

fields.name: measure
fields.doc:
Measures a clip of going down. With `toLowest` the clip is taken only as far as the pelvis gets lowest, which is
for a clip that goes down, does something, and comes back up: its descent is the going-down part.

types.name: HumanDescription
types.doc:
A person's body measurements in metres. Measured from a rig's rest pose by
default; scaledTo() describes the same body at another stature, and
`scale` is then the uniform scale to apply to the character's visual root.
Side-dependent lengths are the mean of both sides.

fields.name: stature
fields.doc: Floor to crown.

fields.name: shoulderWidth
fields.doc: Between the upper arm joints.

fields.name: hipWidth
fields.doc: Between the thigh joints.

fields.name: torso
fields.doc: Pelvis joint to neck joint.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: Uniform scale from the measured rig to this description.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (stature:Float, shoulderWidth:Float, hipWidth:Float, torso:Float, upperArm:Float, forearm:Float, thigh:Float, shin:Float, ?scale:Float):Void

fields.name: measure
fields.doc: Measures a rest pose; stature is the model's rest height (floor to crown).

fields.name: scaledTo
fields.doc: The same body proportions at another stature.

types.name: HumanDisplay
types.doc: How a human is drawn: the skinned mesh, the collision capsules, or the skeleton.

fields.name: parse
fields.doc: Parses "mesh", "capsules", or "skeleton".

types.name: HumanGait
types.doc:
The natural ground speed of a looping locomotion clip. While a foot is
planted it slides backwards past the pelvis at exactly the speed the body
travels, so playing the clip at `speed / naturalSpeed` keeps planted feet
still on the floor. Clips are expected in place, facing +X.

fields.name: naturalSpeed
fields.doc: Metres per second at playback rate 1.

fields.name: startTime
fields.doc:
Seconds into the clip where a walk from standing should begin: the moment in the cycle when the feet are nearest
where they stand at idle, one foot planted under the body and the other passing it. Starting there, the fade from idle
drags the feet a few centimetres; starting at the top of the cycle drags them across a stride.

fields.name: measure
fields.doc:
Measures a clip of asset on rig by sampling one cycle. With `idleClip`, also finds the moment in the cycle
that best matches the feet at idle (see `startTime`); without it a walk starts at the top of the cycle.

types.name: HumanGrip
types.doc: Prop offsets for HumanCharacter.attach, expressed in the standard hand frame (see HumanPose).

fields.name: handle
fields.doc:
A closed-fist grip on a handle. The prop's +X axis runs through the fist
along the hand's thumb side (+Y), held gripPoint metres along the prop from
its origin, and palmDepth metres from the palm centre towards the fingers.

types.name: HumanHand
types.doc:
One hand's fingers, each curled between open (0) and a fist (1). A finger is each child of the
wrist and the single-child chain below it, found from the skeleton so any humanoid rig works. Every
joint of a finger turns about one of its own local axes: negative X on the Quaternius and Mixamo
rigs, which brings the fingertip toward the palm on both hands, and for any other rig the axis that
does, found by turning the knuckle each way in the rest pose and keeping the turn that closes the
finger most. The turns ride on the animation, so fingers keep whatever their clip did and only add
the curl.

fields.name: THUMB
fields.doc: The fingers, in the order curls are given.

fields.name: curl
fields.doc: How curled the hand is now on average, or -1 before the first curl.

fields.name: find
fields.doc: The fingers below a rig's wrist bone, or null when the skeleton has none.

fields.name: has
fields.doc: Whether the hand has this finger.

fields.name: curlOf
fields.doc: How curled a finger is now, or 0 before the first curl.

fields.name: tipPosition
fields.doc: The model-space position of a finger's last joint, or null when the hand lacks the finger.

fields.name: setCurl
fields.doc: Curls every finger alike, 0 open to 1 a fist.

fields.name: setCurls
fields.doc:
Curls each finger on its own: values are indexed THUMB to PINKY, each 0 open to 1 a fist. Fingers
the hand lacks are ignored.

types.name: HumanLimb
types.doc: A limb inverse kinematics can pose: each arm ends at its wrist, each leg at its ankle.

types.name: HumanPosture
types.doc:
Every tuning number behind how a worker holds and moves its body, in one place. The values are in
metres and radians, tuned on the bundled worker rig (`REFERENCE_STATURE` tall); a body built without a
posture scales the lengths to its own stature (`forStature`), and one built with a modified copy carries
itself as that copy says. Nothing here is a fact about a rig's bones, which HumanKit reads from
the skeleton or measures instead.

fields.name: REFERENCE_STATURE
fields.doc: The height of the bundled worker rig the lengths below were tuned on, as its bounds measure it, in metres.

fields.name: comfort
fields.doc: The fraction of arm length (shoulder to wrist) a standing reach uses; the palm adds no reliable length.

fields.name: reachLimit
fields.doc: Beyond this fraction of the arm's length a wrist goal is out of reach.

fields.name: stretch
fields.doc:
How much of the arm's length a worker will stretch to keep clear of a surface's edge, once the lean is
spent: more than the comfortable reach, and short of the limit the solver refuses at.

fields.name: reachSlack
fields.doc:
Reach held back from the stretch when a stance is planned, in metres: the shoulder is measured at one moment
and the grasp point is not exactly the planned one, so a stance planned to the stretch would sometimes be a
little past what the arm can reach.

fields.name: handSpread
fields.doc: With two hands on one object, how far each hand's grasp point sits to its own side of the object's centre, in metres.

fields.name: carryOffset
fields.doc: Where a carried wrist sits relative to the chest bone, in model space (the left hand; the right mirrors Y).

fields.name: carryEaseSeconds
fields.doc: Seconds a hand takes to settle into the carry pose from wherever it was.

fields.name: relaxedCurl
fields.doc: The curl of a resting hand, of one reaching for something, and of one holding it.

fields.name: curlRate
fields.doc: How fast the fingers open and close, in full curls per second.

fields.name: pinchBelow
fields.doc:
A held object thinner than this (across the palm, in metres) is pinched: thumb and index close on it and
the other fingers stay relaxed. The thumb closes this share of the fingers' curl.

fields.name: graspSteps
fields.doc: How many curl steps are measured to find the curl that brings a fingertip to a held object's far side.

fields.name: maxLean
fields.doc: The furthest the upper body leans into a reach, in radians, and how fast it leans.

fields.name: maxHinge
fields.doc: The furthest the body bends forward at the hips, on top of the lean, in radians; used when the lean is not enough to reach across.

fields.name: hingeWithCrouch
fields.doc: Whether a hip hinge may combine with a crouch or a kneel, for a top too deep to reach across from a crouch.

fields.name: hingeDiscomfort
fields.doc: What a stance's hip hinge costs in the planner's comparison of stances, per radian: a hinge is the last resort, after a deeper crouch.

fields.name: reachMargin
fields.doc: How near the arm's limit a reach may end before the planner counts it a stretch, in metres, and what a stretch costs in the comparison of stances.

fields.name: hangSeconds
fields.doc: How long an arm that is not reaching or carrying takes to settle into hanging (and back) while the body leans, and where it hangs under the shoulder.

fields.name: bellyFront
fields.doc: How far the front of the belly sits ahead of the abdomen bone, and the gap left to a surface edge.

fields.name: bellyHalfHeight
fields.doc: How far below the abdomen bone the belly reaches: a belly higher than a surface's top by this much overhangs it without touching it.

fields.name: bellyOverhangMargin
fields.doc: How much higher than that the planner wants the belly before it lets it overhang: leaning lowers the belly a little, and the rule switches a whole edge on or off.

fields.name: blendSpeed
fields.doc:
How fast, in metres per second, a wrist is allowed to go at the peak of the easing as a reach blends in from
the animation or out to it, working from the straight-line distance it has to cover. The wrist follows an arc
and the IK blend is not linear in position, so its real peak is about twice this.

fields.name: lockFeet
fields.doc: Whether a planted foot is held where it is in the world, on a character whose legs are IK chains.

fields.name: lockFrom
fields.doc: The share of the pose that is the idle one above which the feet are held, and the span over which the hold comes in.

fields.name: lockSeconds
fields.doc: Seconds the hold takes to come in and go out.

fields.name: lockReach
fields.doc: How far a held foot may be from where the pose wants it, in metres, before the hold lets go.

fields.name: crouchRate
fields.doc: How fast the body lowers into a crouch and rises out of it, in full crouches per second.

fields.name: legRadius
fields.doc: The radius of a leg, and how far above and below a surface's slab a leg still counts as meeting it (for a kneel).

fields.name: kneelRate
fields.doc: The same for a kneel, which swings an arm down with the body and is taken slower.

fields.name: crouchLevels
fields.doc: How many depths between standing and the full crouch the planner tries, counting both.

fields.name: comfortLean
fields.doc: The lean a worker will put up with before it bends its knees instead, in radians.

fields.name: withdraw
fields.doc: How far the wrists pull back toward the body, and how far they lift.

fields.name: minAhead
fields.doc: The least a withdrawn wrist stays ahead of the chest.

fields.name: standard
fields.doc: The tuning the bundled worker rig was set up with.

fields.name: forStature
fields.doc:
The tuning for a body of `stature` metres: every length, and the speed the wrist may go at, grows with
the body. Angles, fractions of the arm's length, curls and times do not depend on size and are kept.
`edgeGap` is also kept: it is the clearance left to a surface, which is not a matter of the worker's size.

types.name: HumanTargetBox
types.doc: World-space oriented box, with yaw around the vertical Z axis.

types.name: HumanTurn
types.doc:
A turn-in-place clip, measured: how far the body has turned by the end of the clip and how long that takes.
Such a clip turns the body in its own space and does not move the root, so it ends in the pose of the idle
clip turned by that angle. Playing it and then turning the root by the same angle while switching to idle is
seamless, and the feet step through the turn instead of sliding. The turn is read from the line between the
shoulders, which a clip that turns the body turns with it.

fields.name: angle
fields.doc: Radians turned, positive to the left (counter-clockwise from above).

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: Seconds of the clip until the turn is done; the rest of it only holds the pose.

fields.name: measure
fields.doc: Measures a clip, or null when it does not turn the body by roughly a right angle.

types.name: HumanWalker
types.doc:
Walks a HumanCharacter along a route of floor points. The walk clip plays at
the rate that matches the body's speed to the clip's gait, so planted feet
stay on the floor. The body speeds up over the crossfade from idle, slows
down to stop at the end of the route, and turns towards the route at a
bounded rate. rootTransform() is where
to place the character; it faces +X like every AnimKit character.

fields.name: carryGait
fields.doc: The gait of a walk that carries something, when the character has a clip for it; see setCarrying.

fields.name: backGait
fields.doc: The gait of walking backwards, when the character has a clip for it; a retreat uses it.

fields.name: turnLeft
fields.doc: The turn-in-place clips, to the left and to the right, when the character has them; see face.

fields.name: turnRate
fields.doc: Fastest turn, in radians per second.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Measures the walk clip's gait and starts the character idling at the origin.

fields.name: follow
fields.doc:
Walks along points ([x, y] on the floor, metres) at speed, starting at
the first point facing the second. A looping route returns to its start.

fields.name: setCarrying
fields.doc:
Whether the next walk is one that carries something: a character with a carrying walk clip uses it, with
the shoulders and stance of a worker holding a load. It applies from the next route, not the one under way.

fields.name: continueAlong
fields.doc:
Walks along route from where the character stands (the route's first
point), keeping its heading and turning onto the route at turnRate rather
than snapping to it, so what it carries does not swing.

fields.name: retreatAlong
fields.doc: Moves along a retreat route without turning toward it.

fields.name: place
fields.doc: Sets the starting floor pose before a job begins.

fields.name: restart
fields.doc:
Returns to rest at a floor pose as if newly constructed: no route, no turn
pending, and the idle clip playing from its start.

fields.name: face
fields.doc: Turns in place at turnRate, including after a route has ended.

fields.name: turningByClip
fields.doc: Whether a turn clip is turning the body in model space right now (the root takes the turn up when it ends).

fields.name: stanceShare
fields.doc:
How much of the pose showing is the idle one, whose feet are on the floor: 1 standing, 0 in a steady walk, and
in between while the walk fades in or out. A planted foot is held in the world while this is high.

fields.name: settled
fields.doc: Whether the character stands still with its walk faded out: not walking, not turning, not mid-crossfade.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: Stops where the character stands and idles.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: Distance walked along the current route, in metres.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc: Moves along the route and advances the animation by seconds.

fields.name: rootTransform
fields.doc: The character root: standing at the walker's position, turned to its heading.

types.name: LimbControl
types.doc:
One limb of a body: what it was asked to do, and what its IK holds now. The owner sets the asked
mode (reach, carry, or release); `apply` then reconciles the character with it, releasing IK only
when the character still holds something the limb no longer wants. `applied` is the single record of
what the character holds, so there is no flag that can go stale.

fields.name: target
fields.doc: The reach target, and the frame it is given in.

fields.name: curls
fields.doc: The curl of each of this hand's fingers now (HumanHand.THUMB to PINKY); they move toward what the limb's state asks for.

fields.name: carry
fields.doc: Takes up the carry pose, easing in from `from`, the wrist's position now, when there is one.

fields.name: release
fields.doc: Goes back to the animation, releasing the character's IK on the spot.

fields.name: dropIk
fields.doc: Releases the character's IK for this limb without changing what the limb is asked to do.

fields.name: apply
fields.doc:
Brings the character's IK for this limb in line with what it is asked to do; returns whether the
pose changed.

types.name: LimbMode
types.doc: What a limb is being asked to do; Hang is never asked for, it is what a free arm does while the body leans.

fields.name: Free
fields.doc: Follows its animation.

fields.name: Reach
fields.doc: Reaches for a point.

fields.name: Carry
fields.doc: Holds the carry pose at the chest.

fields.name: Hang
fields.doc: An arm not otherwise in use, held hanging under its shoulder.

types.name: PostureState
types.doc:
How far a body is leaned, bent at the hips, crouched and kneeling, and what it has been asked for. Each is a goal
the body eases toward at the rate `HumanPosture` sets, written to the character as it goes. A body that cannot
crouch or kneel (its asset has no clip for it) ignores the ask.

fields.name: setLean
fields.doc: Where the torso is asked to lean; it eases there. Zero stands upright.

fields.name: setHinge
fields.doc: Where the body is asked to bend at the hips, on top of its lean; it eases there. Zero stands straight.

fields.name: setCrouch
fields.doc: Where the body is asked to crouch (0 stands, 1 is the clip's full crouch); it eases there.

fields.name: setKneel
fields.doc:
Where the body is asked to kneel (0 stands, 1 the lowest the kneeling clip goes); it eases there. A kneel and a crouch are
different ways down, so a body kneels only from standing: ask for a crouch of nothing first.

fields.name: crouchAmount
fields.doc: How far the body is into its crouch now.

fields.name: kneelAmount
fields.doc: How far the body is into its kneel now.

fields.name: downAmount
fields.doc: How far down, in either way, the body is now: 0 standing.

fields.name: leanReached
fields.doc: Whether the body has finished easing to the lean and the hinge it was asked for.

fields.name: downReached
fields.doc: Whether the body has finished easing to the crouch and the kneel it was asked for.

fields.name: isBent
fields.doc: Whether the body is, or is on its way to being, leaned, bent or down: the cue for holding a free arm hanging.

fields.name: isKneeling
fields.doc: Whether the body is on a knee or asked to be: a foot cannot be held where it stood then.

fields.name: torsoPitch
fields.doc: How far the upper body is pitched forward now, in radians: the lean and the hip hinge together.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc: Eases each toward its goal over `seconds` and writes the result to the character.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Stands the body upright at once, with nothing asked for.

types.name: ReachSpace
types.doc: The frame a limb's reach target is given in.

fields.name: World
fields.doc: The world: the target stays put while the body moves.

fields.name: Model
fields.doc: The body's root frame: the target moves with the worker's feet but not with its torso.

fields.name: Shoulder
fields.doc: Relative to the limb's shoulder, in the model's axes: the target moves with the shoulder, so the arm keeps its shape as the body walks.

types.name: ApproachFor
types.doc:
Walks to where the limb's shoulder has a comfortable reach to a point and
faces so the point lies straight ahead of that shoulder, before a reach.
The stand-off accounts for the height between shoulder and point: a low
point is approached closer than one at shoulder height.

Given the surface the point lies on, the worker also stands far enough back
that the belly stays clear of its near edge, and leans the upper body
forward over it to keep the shoulder where the reach is comfortable.

fields.name: shortfall
fields.doc:
How far short of the surface's edge the belly ends, in metres, once the lean and the stretch are spent:
zero when the stance clears it. A surface too deep for the arm to reach over (a crouch does not help: it
lowers the shoulder, not carries it over the edge), or a body that cannot crouch at a low one, leaves this above
zero; the job still runs, with the belly over the edge by about this much.

fields.name: crouch
fields.doc: How deep a crouch the worker takes at the stand (0 upright, 1 the clip's full crouch), once it has arrived.

fields.name: kneel
fields.doc: How deep a kneel the worker takes instead of a crouch, for a point too low for one (0 when it does not kneel).

fields.name: lean
fields.doc: How far the upper body leans over the surface at the stand, in radians, once the worker has arrived.

fields.name: hinge
fields.doc: How far it bends at the hips on top of that, for a surface too deep to reach across by leaning alone.

types.name: Carry
types.doc: Establishes a persistent carry posture for subsequent walking actions.

types.name: HumanAction
types.doc: One step of a worker job. Targets supplied by actions are world-space.

types.name: HumanActionBase
types.doc: Common completion and failure state for concrete actions.

types.name: HumanReachPhase
types.doc: Phase of a HumanReachTask's walk-then-reach sequence.

types.name: HumanReachTask
types.doc: Legacy walk, reach, wait, and release convenience task.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
The legacy target remains in model space. The composed job's walk uses
floor-world points; its reach uses Reach.inModelSpace.

types.name: Pick

fields.name: object
fields.doc: The box of the object being picked up, so the fingers close to its size; null for the plain grip.

fields.name: grip
fields.doc: Becomes true for one full-weight tick at the grasp point.

fields.name: pickError
fields.doc: Largest palm distance from its grasp point when the hands closed, in metres.

types.name: Place
types.doc:
Places what the hands hold at target, then opens and withdraws the hands.
With a held-point provider (HumanBody.setHeldPoint, set by the simulation
layer while a hand holds an object), target is where the object's reference
point goes and the wrists are solved to put it there; without one, target is
where the palms go. The object keeps the orientation it was carried with.

fields.name: grip
fields.doc: False once the part should be released by the simulation layer.

fields.name: atTarget
fields.doc: True after the hands have reached the placing point.

fields.name: placementError
fields.doc: Distance from the placed point to target when the hands opened, in metres.

types.name: PlayClip
types.doc: Crossfades to a named clip and plays it for a fixed duration.

types.name: Press
types.doc: Reaches a button, holds contact briefly, and releases the arm.

types.name: Reach
types.doc: Ramps one limb's IK toward a world point.

fields.name: inModelSpace
fields.doc: Keeps HumanReachTask's historical model-space target semantics.

types.name: ReleaseLimb
types.doc: Ramps an active IK limb back onto its animation.

fields.name: ramp
fields.doc: The shortest the release takes; it lasts longer when the hand has far to go, to keep its speed down.

types.name: Stance
types.doc: Where a worker stands and how it holds its body to reach a point: what StancePlanner weighs between.

types.name: StancePlanner
types.doc:
Chooses where a worker stands, how it faces and how it holds its body (crouched or kneeling, leaned, bent at the hips) to
reach a point with one arm or two, optionally over a surface it has to keep its belly and knees clear of.

Standing is tried first. A worker crouches only for a point lower than the arm comfortably reaches below the shoulder:
crouching brings the shoulder down, not forward over a surface, so it does nothing for a point at table height. For a
lower one, ever deeper crouches are tried and the first that is easy is taken; failing that, the least hard of those
tried. A point lower than a crouch reaches is taken from a knee instead, if that is clearly the easier stance. How hard
a stance is has one measure (`discomfort`), so every comparison below uses the same one.

fields.name: plan
fields.doc: The stance to take, or one whose `failure` says why there is none.

types.name: Wait
types.doc: Keeps the current animation and IK pose for a fixed duration.

types.name: WalkTo
types.doc: Walks to one floor point, or along an explicit sequence of floor points.

fields.name: deferred
fields.doc: Resolve a destination from the worker's pose when this action starts.

types.name: FacilityFetchJob
types.doc: A fetch plan resolved into one HumanJob when its delivery is named.

fields.name: deliver
fields.doc:
The job: fetch the part from its slot, walk the lane, set it down at `placePoint`. The worker leans
over the rack's and the station's tops and closes its fingers to the part's size when the facility
describes them (a rack's and station's `surface`, a slot's `itemHalfExtents`); a caller may pass
`rackSurface`, `stationSurface`, or `part` to override or supply what the facility does not. With
neither, the worker stands where its shoulder reaches the point and grips plainly.

Without a `placePoint` the part is set down at the middle of the station's surface, resting on it: the point
is the surface's top plus half the part's height, so the facility must describe both.

types.name: FacilityJobs
types.doc: Creates lane-following worker jobs from named facility targets.

types.name: FacilityTargets
types.doc: Resolves facility IDs into positions in their shared facility frame.

fields.name: surfaceBox
fields.doc: The top of a rack or station as a box in the facility frame, or null when the facility describes none.

fields.name: slotItemBox
fields.doc: The box of the item a rack slot holds, in the facility frame, or null when the facility does not say.

types.name: FacilityWalk
types.doc:
Bridges AutomationKit's facility routing to HumanWalker. HumanKit itself
does not depend on RobotKit or AutomationKit; this small package is the
one place that knows about both, so a person can walk a FacilityRoute (or
any robotkit Path) planned above it.

fields.name: routeFromPath
fields.doc:
Floor points ([x, y], metres) along path's waypoints in order, for
HumanWalker.follow. Consecutive waypoints closer than a millimetre are
collapsed, so a route never carries a zero-length final segment that
would leave the walker's ending heading undefined.

fields.name: routeFromFacilityRoute
fields.doc: Floor points along a facility route's path, from its origin to its destination station.

types.name: HumanJob
types.doc: Ordered actions for one body. A failed action stops the job.

fields.name: bind
fields.doc: Binds an unstarted job to a simulated body.

fields.name: orderedActions
fields.doc: Read-only copy of the ordered actions, for physics bindings.

fields.name: abort
fields.doc: Stops the job with a failure found outside its actions, such as by a simulation layer.

types.name: HumanJobBuilder
types.doc: Resolves a portable job spec into world-space HumanKit actions.

types.name: HumanJobSpec
types.doc: Strict, versioned description of an editor-authored human job.

types.name: HumanJobStep
types.doc: Typed canonical step. Action-specific requirements are enforced by parse.

types.name: HumanJobTarget
types.doc: Validated target in a canonical job step.

types.name: ArmQuality
types.doc: What a run of poses did to one arm, in model space (+Z up, +X forward).

types.name: MotionQuality
types.doc:
Measures how natural a motion is from its poses, one sample per tick: arms that flip, fold up to
the shoulder, bend too sharply, whip, or are dragged behind the torso. A motion's tests can
hold these to limits, and a regression then shows up as a number.

fields.name: sample
fields.doc: Adds the pose reached `seconds` after the previous sample (any value the first time).

fields.name: breakContinuity
fields.doc: Forgets the previous sample, so a jump the caller caused (a reset) is not counted as motion.

types.name: Naturalness
types.doc:
What a run of poses looks like from the floor up, sampled once per tick: whether planted feet slide, whether the
centre of mass stays over the feet while both are down, and how jerky the pelvis and wrists are.
`MotionQuality` judges the arms; this judges the body. Neither says a motion is natural, only that a regression
showed up as a number.

A foot is planted from when it is low (within `PLANTED_HEIGHT` of where it first stood) and slow (under
`PLANTED_SPEED`) for `PLANTED_SAMPLES` samples running, until it lifts or speeds up (a swing foot skimming the
floor is fast, so is not taken for planted). Its slide is how far it moves from where it was planted while it stays
so. The centre of mass is a weighted mean of a few bones, and the support polygon is the hull of both feet from
heel to toe; the margin is how far inside it the mass projects (negative outside), kept only while both feet are planted.

fields.name: PLANTED_SPEED
fields.doc: Slower than this a low foot is planted; faster than `UNPLANTED_SPEED` it has left the floor.

fields.name: maxSlide
fields.doc: The furthest a foot moved from where it was planted while it stayed planted, in metres.

fields.name: maxSlideAt
fields.doc: The sample at which that furthest slide was reached, and the one at which that foot was planted.

fields.name: slideTotal
fields.doc: The slide of every plant added up, in metres, and the seconds a foot was planted.

fields.name: minSupportMargin
fields.doc: Least margin of the centre of mass inside the feet's support, in metres, while both were planted; infinite if never.

fields.name: floorPenetration
fields.doc: Lowest a foot went below where it first stood, in metres (positive: it went into the floor).

fields.name: maxPelvisJerk
fields.doc: Largest jerk of the pelvis and of either wrist, in metres per second cubed.

fields.name: maxFootTilt
fields.doc: The most a planted foot tilted from the way it first stood (ankle to toe, pitched up or down), in degrees.

fields.name: maxFootJerk
fields.doc: Largest jerk of either ankle: a foot held in the world and let go again must not pop.

fields.name: standOnTheFloorOf
fields.doc:
Takes the floor under each foot from another run's: a foot's floor height is taken from its first sample, which is only
right when the run begins with both feet down. A run that begins mid-stride says so by taking it from one that stood.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: One line for a report.

types.name: HumanActor
types.doc:
A person taking part in a SimKit session: the body proxy's capsules as one
kinematic actor. The person pushes whatever they walk into and nothing
pushes them back. Poses are keyframes in simulation time: a writer pushes
one per tick, for the tick about to complete.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Joins a stopped session with the body at a pose, through a root transform.

fields.name: pushPose
fields.doc: Where the body is at simulation time `time`.

types.name: HumanWorker
types.doc: A job-driven animated worker and its physical capsule actor.

fields.name: maxHoldDistance
fields.doc: Farthest an object's origin may be from the hand's grip point when a hold starts, in metres.

fields.name: bindPick
fields.doc: Associates a Pick with a dynamic object and its world grasp point.

fields.name: bindPlace
fields.doc: Associates a Place with the object to release at its world target.

fields.name: runSpec
fields.doc: Resolves a document job and binds its dynamic parts to the session.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc:
Returns the worker to where its session starts. The session's own reset has
already put its objects, actors and stabilisers back; this restores what
lives beside the session: the body at its start pose with nothing reaching,
carried or held, every hold and pin forgotten, and a document job started
again from its first step. A job given to run() cannot be rewound, so that
worker stands idle at its start pose.

fields.name: approachShortfall
fields.doc:
The most any approach in the current job fell short of standing clear of its surface, in metres: above
zero where the reach needs a crouch the body does not do. See `ApproachFor.shortfall`.

fields.name: currentActionLabel
fields.doc: What the job is doing now, in a word, for reports: the running action's kind, or "idle".

fields.name: currentStep
fields.doc: Zero-based document step currently running, or null for an empty or finished job.

fields.name: addRobotLink
fields.doc: A robot link's collision bound is approximated by a sphere around its body origin.

fields.name: addRobotLinkPose
fields.doc: Samples a robot runtime link's collision center after each physics tick.

fields.name: advance
fields.doc:
Call once before every tick of the session, however the session is driven
(`SimSession.stepPaced` from the owner's loop, or `step`). The job and the
actor pose run one tick ahead: the pose for the tick about to complete, and
the pin, hold and release events that belong to it, land before it runs.

fields.name: handBody
fields.doc: The session body of a hand's collision capsule, which carries what that hand holds.

fields.name: readSignals
fields.doc:
What the body is touching or near as of the last tick: the zones it stands in and its distance to each tracked
link. Reading captures the physics world, so a display asks when it draws; `onTick` is for a reader that wants
every tick.

types.name: HumanWorkerSignals
types.doc: Safety sample from one completed simulation tick. Distances are metres.

types.name: HumanZone
types.doc: A floor polygon in session world metres.
